bib.title: Exploiting Cloze Questions for Few Shot Text Classification and Natural Language Inference
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 16th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL), pages 255-269

question: Can task descriptions given as cloze-style patterns be combined with supervised training to beat standard fine-tuning and semi-supervised methods when only a few labeled examples exist?
hypothesis: Providing a task description (pattern plus verbalizer) lets a pretrained masked LM understand the task from few examples, so PET outperforms supervised training in low-resource settings.
contributions: Pattern-Exploiting Training (PET): semi-supervised procedure reformulating inputs as cloze questions, finetuning one MLM per pattern, soft-labeling unlabeled data with the ensemble, training a standard classifier
iPET: iterative variant training generations on growing self-labeled sets, usable zero-shot
Automatic verbalizer search (AVS) in Appendix E
Experiments on four English datasets and multilingual x-stance

method.summary: Each input is converted by a pattern into a cloze question with one mask, and a verbalizer maps labels to vocabulary words; an MLM is finetuned per pattern-verbalizer pair on the small labeled set (with auxiliary MLM loss alpha=1e-4). The ensemble soft-labels unlabeled data (temperature 2) and a sequence classifier is trained on it; iPET repeats this over generations with training sets growing by factor 5.

datasets.name: Yelp Review Full
datasets.split: T = first t/|L| examples per label of train set (t in 10,50,100,1000); D = 10,000 unlabeled per label; official test set
datasets.preprocessing: \n replaced by space; truncated to 256 tokens (longest first) before applying patterns

datasets.name: MNLI
datasets.size: 10000 / 10000 (m/mm) examples, dev set used for reporting
datasets.split: as Yelp; evaluated on dev set because of the 2 submissions per 14 hours limit

datasets.name: x-stance
datasets.split: 1000/2000/4000 subsets or full; with full sets D=T; Italian zero-shot cross-lingual

training.objective: L = (1-alpha)*L_CE + alpha*L_MLM per PVP, alpha=1e-4; final classifier trained on soft labels (softmax temperature T=2)
training.optimizer: inferred: Adam-type (adam epsilon 1e-8 in Table 5, Transformers defaults)
training.batch_size: 16 effective (per GPU batch 4 x 4 gradient accumulation steps); PET with LM: 1 labeled + 3 unlabeled per batch
training.steps: PET model 250 (1000 with auxiliary LM); final classifier C 5000; supervised 250; x-stance 3 epochs; in-domain PT 50000
training.hardware: single NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti 11GB; in-domain pretraining on 3 GTX 1080 Ti
training.compute: PET model 250 steps ~30 min; with LM 1000 steps ~60 min; labeling D 15-30 min per model; classifier C 5000 steps ~2 h
training.seeds: 3 seeds per model; ensemble of n PVPs has 3n models

other.iPET: lambda=0.25, d=5, k=ceil(log_d(1000/|T|)) generations until each model saw >=1000 examples
other.weighting: w(p) uniform or training-set accuracy before training (weighted default)

inference.decoding: label with highest masked-token score after softmax over verbalizer words
inference.samples: 3 runs per configuration, mean and std reported
inference.prompting: cloze pattern with one mask plus verbalizer; no in-context examples

parameters.AVS: k=250, epsilon=1e-3, i_max=5, m=10, tokens with >=2 alphabetic chars, 10000 most frequent in D
parameters.iPET zero-shot: M0 untrained, c1(l)=10/|L|, sample from the top 100 examples per label

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct on test set (MNLI dev)

metrics.name: macro-F1 (x-stance)
metrics.definition: macro-average of F1 for labels 0 and 1, official script

eval.protocol: three seeds, mean +- std; no dev set for hyperparameters; first-t/|L| examples used as T so not resampled

prompts.text: a. All in all, it was <MASK>.
a || In summary, the restaurant is <MASK>.

evidence.quote: We use a learning rate of 1 · 10−5, a batch size of 16

results.claim: With 10 labeled examples on Yelp, PET reaches 52.9 accuracy while supervised fine-tuning gets 21.1 (near chance).
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, |T|=10, 10,000 unlabeled per label
results.table: Table 1, row |T|=10 PET, column Yelp (supervised row 21.1)

results.claim: On MNLI-m with 100 examples PET gets 74.7 versus 47.9 supervised; iPET reaches 78.4.
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, MNLI matched, |T|=100

results.claim: Zero-shot iPET on AG's News (87.5) beats supervised training with 1000 examples (86.9).
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, |T|=0 (iPET zero-shot, 10 examples per generation-1 label split), AG's News
results.quote: on AG’s News, it even performs better than standard supervised training with 1000 examples

results.claim: Unsupervised single patterns vary widely: on Yelp avg 33.8 vs best-on-test pattern 40.8, so pattern choice matters without a dev set.
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, |T|=0, no training; max is the pattern best on the test set
results.table: Table 1, rows unsupervised (avg) and (max), column Yelp

results.claim: With only 10 examples, PET on Yelp (52.9) exceeds the best individual pattern after finetuning (52.4); gap between worst (39.6) and best pattern is large.
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, |T|=10
results.table: Table 4, rows min 39.6, max 52.4, PET weighted 52.9, column Yelp

results.claim: Distilling the ensemble into one classifier beats the undistilled ensemble on Yelp (52.9 vs 51.7); uniform vs weighted weighting shows no clear difference (52.7 vs 52.9).
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, |T|=10
results.table: Table 4, rows PET (no distillation) 51.7, PET uniform 52.7, PET weighted 52.9, column Yelp

results.claim: PET and iPET beat UDA and MixText with RoBERTa base at 10 examples (Yelp: PET 48.8, iPET 52.9, UDA 27.3, MixText 20.4).
results.setup: RoBERTa base, Yelp, |T|=10; UDA/MixText steps tuned on the test set (favourable to them)
results.note: Single run values, no std reported

results.claim: On x-stance German with 1000 examples PET gets 66.4 F1 vs 43.3 supervised; the gap shrinks to 77.9 vs 76.6 on the full German set.
results.setup: XLM-R base, x-stance, macro-average F1 of labels 0 and 1, three runs

results.claim: Handcrafted verbalizers beat automatic verbalizer search: Yelp 60.0 vs 55.2 with 50 examples, though AVS still beats supervised (44.8).
results.setup: RoBERTa large (355M), Yelp/AG's/Yahoo/MNLI, three seeds, mean accuracy, |T|=50; AVS k=250, eps=1e-3, i_max=5, m=10
results.table: Table 7, row PET + AVS, column Yelp (PET 60.0, supervised 44.8)

results.claim: The auxiliary language-modeling loss helps most at 10 examples and becomes less important or harmful with more data.
results.setup: RoBERTa large, four English datasets, |T| in 10/50/100/1000 (Fig 3, values not in text)
results.quote: the auxiliary task is extremely valuable when training on just 10 examples

results.claim: Skipping iPET generations 2-3 (annotating 10*5^4 examples straight from M1) gives worse accuracy than gradual growth.
results.setup: Zero-shot iPET on AG's News and Yahoo (Fig 4)
results.quote: this clearly leads to worse performance

results.claim: Training one PET model for 250 steps took about 30 minutes on one GTX 1080 Ti; the final classifier for 5000 steps took 2 hours.
results.setup: single NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti 11GB, RoBERTa large
results.quote: Training a single PET classiﬁer for 250 steps on one GPU took approximately 30 minutes

limits: Needs a task expressible as patterns, and hand-written patterns and verbalizers; AVS does worse than manual verbalizers and fails on 3 of 10 Yahoo labels and all MNLI labels
Requires a large unlabeled in-domain set D (10,000 per label)
UDA and MixText compared at RoBERTa base with steps tuned on the test set; one supervised MNLI run (|T|=1000) excluded as underfit
Number of iPET iterations beyond the tested ones not explored
In-domain pretraining checked on Yelp only
Gains shrink as |T| grows (no AG's News advantage at 1000)
Uses finetuned masked LMs with gradient updates, not in-context prompting of a frozen generative LM

terms.definition: a function P that takes x as input and outputs a phrase or sentence P(x) that contains exactly one mask token, i.e., its output can be viewed as a cloze question
an injective function v : L -> V that maps each label to a word from M's vocabulary

figures.caption: PET for sentiment classification. (1) A number of patterns encoding some form of task description are created to convert training examples to cloze questions; for each pattern, a pretrained language model is finetuned. (2) The ensemble of trained models annotates unlabeled data. (3) A classifier is trained on the resulting soft-labeled dataset.
